description:
FILED s534a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) from the profile of the new bench rows (docs/method-lookup-eval-s534.md §2).  PRE-EXISTING on main 95a1de03.

MECHANISM: `%p-isa-symbol` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the overload section, "PKG's @ISA symbol for an inheritance reader") is

    (let ((sym (find-symbol "@isa" pkg)))
      (and sym (not (gethash sym *p-stash-deleted*)) sym))

and `*p-stash-deleted*` is `(make-hash-table :test 'eq :weakness :key)`.  Every SBCL weak-table operation runs under `sb-thread::call-with-recursive-system-lock` + without-interrupts, and this one runs once per class an @ISA walk passes: in p-method-call's prologue and its `find-in-class`, in `%p-isa-parent-names` (the overload walks), `%pcl-find-method-in-chain` (can / SUPER::), `%pcl-find-autoload-in-isa`, `%pcl-isa-ancestry`.  Its sibling `%p-stash-deleted-p` (the inline helper defined beside the table) already guards the same table with `(plusp (hash-table-count ...))` -- `%p-isa-symbol` is the one reader that does not.

MEASURED (sb-sprof, base 95a1de03, scratch/s534a/prof/base-*.prof): gethash/weak + the system lock = 19.1 % of methinh3, 11.2 % of methinh, 11.4 % of methpoly, 18.2 % of ovlbool.

FIX SHAPE (one line, answer-identical): `(not (%p-stash-deleted-p sym))` in place of the bare gethash -- an empty table answers NIL either way.  Prototype: scratch/s534a/rt/proto-d.lisp (mk-proto-d.pl) in the s534a worktree; its A/B is in the evaluation doc.  The deeper half is #4501's: a program that EVER deletes a stash entry (namespace::clean, YAML::Tiny's `delete $YAML::Tiny::{refaddr}`, Moo's cleanups) makes the count non-zero for the rest of the run and the lock comes back; *p-stash-deleted* need not be weak at all -- its keys are INTERNED symbols, which their package keeps alive, so `:weakness :key` buys nothing and costs the lock (decide that in #4501).

BAR: the methinh / methinh3 / methpoly / ovlbool rows BEFORE -> AFTER through `heavy.sh <label> bench` (`BENCH_RT_B` A/B); `Pl/t/method-dispatch-01.t`, `Pl/t/method-cache-01.t` and the stash-delete guards (grep -l stash-deleted Pl/t); gate + sweep (a cl/ change).  If #4523 (the inherited cache) lands first, its HIT path no longer calls %p-isa-symbol, but every miss, `can`, `isa`, `SUPER::` and overload walk still does -- this stays worth its line.
subject: PERF: `%p-isa-symbol` asks the WEAK table *p-stash-deleted* on EVERY @ISA read with no count guard -- SBCL takes its global system lock per weak-table operation: 11-19 % of an inherited method call (lever (d) of the s534a evaluation; the dispatch-path overlap of #4501)
